thread:
tom: Hey team — just got married over the weekend! Quick q: how do I add my spouse to benefits mid‑year and when will coverage start?

maria (People Ops): Congrats Tom!!! :tada: You can add a spouse as a qualifying life event. We need the marriage certificate and spouse SSN. Are you on Redwood’s benefits portal (Workday)?

tom: Yeah I have access. Is there a deadline window for submitting the docs? Don’t want any gap.

alex (Benefits): Hi — welcome to married life :) You have 30 days from the date of marriage to submit for a retro effective date. If submitted within 30 days, coverage can be effective back to the marriage date (subject to carrier rules). If after 30 days, the earliest effective date is the 1st of the next month after enrollment.

tom: Good to know. What format for docs? PDF ok?

maria (People Ops): PDF is perfect. Please upload scanned marriage certificate (or certified copy) and spouse SSN card or passport. Redact any unrelated info.

alex (Benefits): Steps:```1) Login to Benefits Portal (Workday) -> Change Life Events 2) Select "Marriage / Add Spouse" 3) Upload docs (marriage cert + SSN) 4) Submit and confirm dependent details 5) Watch for confirmation email from hr-bot``` Payroll cutoff note: enrollments must be submitted before payroll cutoff (15th) for changes to appear on the next month's paycheck.

hr-bot: Automated reminder — Benefit change request received? Make sure to complete upload. Missing docs will delay processing. Link: https://benefits.redwood.example/portal

tom: If I want dental + health, do I pick both in the same flow?

alex (Benefits): Yes — choose each plan you want during the life event flow. Plan premiums will pro-rate back to the event date if eligible. You can also opt for only dental now and add health later, but that may affect rates.

sana: Also fyi — FSA/HSA rules: if you enroll mid-year for HSA-eligible plan, payroll contributions will be pro‑rated. Talk to Benefits if you plan large deposits.

tom: Thanks. One more — spouse works and has coverage through their employer. Can we do dual coverage?

maria (People Ops): Yes you can elect Redwood coverage if spouse has employer coverage, but check coordination of benefits and premium impact. If spouse's plan is primary, claims routing may differ. Alex can send the COB info.

alex (Benefits): Right — we’ll attach the COB form after enrollment. If spouse has other coverage, upload that carrier info or a copy of their insurance card so carriers can set primary/secondary.

tom: Perfect. I’ll upload docs tonight. Appreciate the rapid help!

maria (People Ops): Great — ping here if anything gets stuck. Once processed, you’ll get a confirmation email with effective dates and payroll adjustments. :thumbsup:

hr-bot: Enrollment processed (pending carrier verification). Expect final confirmation within 3–10 business days.

tom: Got the pending message, thanks.

sana: Congrats again!!
